question: Should commercial recordings disclose when a singer's vocal has been pitch-corrected?
answer: Listeners judge singers partly on singing in tune, and buy tickets on it. Silent correction sells a skill the performer may lack, much as undisclosed retouching sells a body that does not exist; France has required labels on retouched commercial photos of models since 2017. A plain credit would tell audiences what they are praising.
move: Whichever side you took, it turns on whether records document performances or build them.
ask: Where do I quietly polish things so people think I am better at something than I am?
counterpoint: Records have always been assembled: tape splices, retakes, the best syllables comped from twenty takes, reverb from rooms that never existed. Pitch correction is one more edit, routine in commercial pop, so a label would sit on nearly everything and tell nobody anything. The concert stage already exists as the test of raw skill.
reference: Décret n° 2017-738 du 4 mai 2017 relatif aux photographies à usage commercial, Journal officiel de la République française, 2017
